description: The simplest structure PyBigDFT accepts: a dictionary with `units` and a list of one-key dictionaries, element -> [x, y, z]. It goes as `posinp=` to the calculator, which writes it inside NAME.yaml under the key `posinp`.
intent: Describe a molecule as a dictionary of positions and pass it to a calculation.
output:
<BigDFT> log of the run will be written in logfile: ./log-water.yaml
atoms: 3 | orbitals: 4

description: `IO.read_xyz` takes an OPEN FILE, not a file name. `fragmentation` is "atomic" (one fragment per atom, the default) or "single" (the whole file is one fragment); nothing else is accepted.
intent: Read a structure from an .xyz file into a System, and turn it into `posinp`.

description: `posinp=` also accepts a file name. The calculator then refers to that file instead of writing the positions in NAME.yaml, so the .xyz must travel with the input: prefer a dictionary (system.get_posinp()) when the input is sent elsewhere.
intent: Give the name of an .xyz file directly as the structure of a calculation.
output:
<BigDFT> log of the run will be written in logfile: ./log-from_file.yaml
structure read from: h2o.xyz

description: A System is a dictionary of Fragments; a Fragment is a list of Atoms. Fragment names have the form "NAME:NUMBER". An Atom is made from a dictionary holding the element as key, its position, and the units of that position.
intent: Build a System atom by atom, grouped in named fragments.
output:
valence electrons of the fragment: 8.0
first atom: O [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]

description: `Molecule(name)` is already a `posinp` dictionary (units, positions): pass it as it is to a calculator. It is not a System; build one from its positions when fragments or geometry operations are needed.
intent: Take a common molecule from the database shipped with PyBigDFT.
output:
positions: ['O', 'H', 'H']
as a System, fragments: ['molecule:0']

description: Fragment.translate takes a vector in BOHR, whatever the units the atoms were given in. `centroid` is in bohr too. Multiply by AU_to_A to get angstroem.
intent: Translate and rotate a fragment, and measure a distance between fragments.
output:
distance between the two molecules: 3.000 angstroem
atoms in the dimer: 6

description: The boundary conditions come from the cell, not from an input variable. In a `posinp` dictionary the key `cell` holds the three lengths; a free direction is written `inf` (a surface is periodic along x and z, free along y). No `cell` key at all means an isolated system.
intent: Give a periodic cell to a structure: bulk, surface or isolated.
output:
<BigDFT> log of the run will be written in logfile: ./log-si.yaml
periodic
surface
k-point mesh read by BigDFT: [2, 2, 2]

description: `IO.write_xyz` takes a System and an OPEN FILE. The first line holds the number of atoms and the units, the second the boundary conditions.
intent: Write a System to an .xyz file.

description: `log.astruct` is the `posinp` dictionary BigDFT read. Build a System from it with system_from_dict_positions. (Systems.system_from_log does the same in one call but imports scipy, which fails in the BigDFT 1.9.1 image of the pack.)
intent: Recover the structure a calculation was run on, from its log.
output:
system_from_log is unusable in this image: libifport.so.5: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
units: angstroem | atoms: ['O', 'H', 'H']

description: An Inputfile is a dictionary. Its methods (set_xc, set_hgrid, ...) are the functions of BigDFT.InputActions, attached when the object is created: they do not appear in dir(Inputfile). Each one writes one or a few keys; printing the Inputfile shows exactly what BigDFT will read. A key left out keeps BigDFT's default.
intent: Write the three settings every calculation needs: functional, grid spacing, extent of the grid.

description: spin_polarize(mpol) writes dft.nspin = 2 and dft.mpol = number of up minus down electrons. charge(q) writes dft.qcharge: +1 for a cation (charge() without argument means -1, an anion). The parity of mpol must match the number of electrons, or BigDFT refuses the input.
intent: Set the spin polarisation and the charge of a system.
output:
<BigDFT> log of the run will be written in logfile: ./log-cation.yaml
charge: 1 | nspin: 2 | mpol: 1

description: set_scf_convergence(gnrm=...) writes dft.gnrm_cv (default 1e-4). Called WITHOUT a value it writes the string "default", not a number. The iteration limits are dft.itermax (50 per cycle) and dft.nrepmax (1 restart): a spin-polarised or difficult system often needs more than 50.
intent: Tighten the self-consistency criterion and allow more iterations.
output: {'dft': {'gnrm_cv': 1e-05, 'itermax': 200, 'nrepmax': 5}, 'lin_general': {'rpnrm_cv': 'default'}, 'mix': {'rpnrm_cv': 'default'}}

description: optimize_geometry writes the `geopt` section. Its default method is FIRE with 50 steps and forcemax = 0, which means "stop on the fluctuation of the forces": give forcemax (Ha/bohr) explicitly. SQNM is the usual choice for molecules.
intent: Ask for a geometry optimisation.
output:
<BigDFT> log of the run will be written in logfile: ./log-relax.yaml
{'method': 'SQNM', 'ncount_cluster_x': 100, 'betax': 4.0, 'frac_fluct': 1.0, 'forcemax': 0.001}

description: BigDFT has no pseudopotential registered for a hybrid functional. With set_xc("PBE0") alone it refuses the input: 'The pseudopotential parameter file "psppar.O" is lacking, and no registered pseudo found for "O"'. Tell it to use the PBE ones (XC code 11), for every element of the structure. BigDFT then warns that the pseudopotential was generated with another functional.
intent: Use a hybrid functional (PBE0, B3LYP, HF): name the pseudopotentials explicitly.
output:
<BigDFT> log of the run will be written in logfile: ./log-pbe0_refused.yaml
STOP  MPIFAKE: MPI_ABORT
 <BigDFT> log of the run will be written in logfile: ./log-pbe0.yaml
without pseudopotentials: The pseudopotential parameter file "psppar.O" is lacking, and no registered pseudo found for "O"
with the PBE pseudopotentials: dry run passed, memory peak 86 MB

description: The Inputfile is a dictionary of sections. Any variable of BigDFT can be written as inp[section][key] = value; create the section first if it is not there. Actions and direct keys mix freely. A wrong key name is NOT refused by PyBigDFT: only BigDFT (the dry run) tells.
intent: Set an input variable that no action covers, by writing its key.
output:
<BigDFT> log of the run will be written in logfile: ./log-keys.yaml
ncong read by BigDFT: 8 | alphamix: 0.3

description: set_implicit_solvent() switches the cavity on with the parameters of water. It takes no solvent name in PyBigDFT 0.9: another solvent is set by writing the keys of psolver.environment (epsilon, and the cavity parameters).
intent: Compute in implicit solvent (soft-sphere cavity).
output:
<BigDFT> log of the run will be written in logfile: ./log-solvated.yaml
no solvent name: set_implicit_solvent() got an unexpected keyword argument 'solvent'
cavity: soft-sphere | epsilon: 24.852

description: Three independent actions, each writing one key. The field is in atomic units (Ha/bohr). The dispersion correction (D3) only exists for isolated systems.
intent: Add an electric field, a dispersion correction, or an electronic temperature.

description: These actions choose what a run leaves in data-NAME/ besides its log.
intent: Ask BigDFT to write the density, the orbitals or cube files.
output: {'dft': {'output_denspot': 21, 'nplot': 2}, 'output': {'orbitals': 'binary'}}

description: An Inputfile is a dictionary: yaml.dump writes it, Inputfile(dictionary) reads it. The file NAME.yaml that a calculator writes is the same thing plus `posinp`.
intent: Save an Inputfile to YAML and load it back.
output:
dft:
  hgrids: 0.4
  ixc: PBE

description: extract_virtual_states(nvirt) writes dft.nvirt and dft.norbv. Without it a log only holds the occupied levels.
intent: Compute empty (virtual) orbitals, for a gap or a density of states above the Fermi level.
output:
<BigDFT> log of the run will be written in logfile: ./log-virtual.yaml
{'ixc': 'PBE', 'norbv': -4, 'nvirt': 4, 'itermax_virt': 150}

description: A dry run (SystemCalculator(dry_run=True)) makes BigDFT read the input and build the grid, without any SCF step. It writes NAME.yaml, the file a real run reads. PyBigDFT returns a Logfile and raises nothing, WHATEVER BigDFT said. Three outcomes, all read in log.log: - refused: the key "Additional Info" is at the top of the log, with the reason; - accepted with errors: "List of error found while parsing input variables" is there. BigDFT went on although a value is out of range or not allowed; - accepted: neither key. Warnings, if any, are under "WARNINGS". The memory estimate (log.memory_peak) is only printed for the cubic algorithm: do not use it as the test.
intent: Dry-run an input and decide, correctly, whether BigDFT accepted it.
output:
<BigDFT> log of the run will be written in logfile: ./log-good.yaml
 <BigDFT> log of the run will be written in logfile: ./log-odd.yaml
 <BigDFT> log of the run will be written in logfile: ./log-hybrid.yaml
STOP  MPIFAKE: MPI_ABORT
 <BigDFT> log of the run will be written in logfile: ./log-typo.yaml
STOP  MPIFAKE: MPI_ABORT
 <BigDFT> log of the run will be written in logfile: ./log-coarse.yaml
good        : accepted
odd         : accepted, warnings: ['Odd number of electrons, no closed shell system']
hybrid      : refused, The pseudopotential parameter file "psppar.O" is lacking, and no registered pseudo found for "O"
typo        : refused, An invalid key (hgrid) has been found in section "dft". Check above the allowed keys.
out of range: accepted WITH ERRORS, hgrids = '9.0' not in range.

description: A dry run writes log-NAME.yaml, like a real run. Under the same name and in the same directory it REPLACES the log of the finished calculation, and the energy is gone. `skip=True` does not protect: with dry_run=True the estimate runs anyway. Test for a finished calculation yourself before preparing it again.
intent: Never dry-run under the name of a calculation that is already done.
output:
<BigDFT> log of the run will be written in logfile: ./log-h2o.yaml
 <BigDFT> Logfile existing, renamed into: ./logfiles/log-h2o.07:55:57.381.yaml
before: energy -17.209856430993852
after : log-h2o.yaml is now a dry-run log, without energy

description: The HAPS runs `bigdft -n NAME` on NAME.yaml and nothing else. So: write every input with a dry run in one directory, keep the names that passed, and hand them to haps_bigdft(names=[...], directory="runs"). A run name may only hold letters, digits, '_' and '-' (no dot, no colon). Keep it to 30 characters: the HAPS accepts 64, but the dry run of BigDFT truncates the name of the log at 30 and PyBigDFT then finds no log and returns None.
intent: Prepare several runs for the HAPS: one NAME.yaml each, dry-run, names it accepts.
output:
<BigDFT> log of the run will be written in logfile: ./log-water_h050.yaml
 <BigDFT> log of the run will be written in logfile: ./log-water_h045.yaml
 <BigDFT> log of the run will be written in logfile: ./log-water_h040.yaml
 <BigDFT> log of the run will be written in logfile: ./log-water_grid_convergence_study_h.yaml
STOP  MPIFAKE: MPI_ABORT
a name of 32 characters: the dry run returns None, its log was written under a truncated name
ready for the HAPS: ['water_h050', 'water_h045', 'water_h040']
next: haps_bigdft(names=['water_h050', 'water_h045', 'water_h040'], directory="runs")

description: A Dataset holds runs identified by a dictionary (`id`). `run()` executes them with the calculator given to append_run, `fetch_results(attribute=...)` returns the attribute of every log, in order. The run names are built from the ids ("h:0.5"): they contain ':' and '.', which the HAPS does not accept. Use a Dataset for dry runs and local runs; name the runs yourself for the HAPS.

description: Logfile(path) loads log-NAME.yaml. Its attributes (energy, nat, fermi_level, dipole, forces, evals, memory_peak, ...) are created from the content of the log: one that BigDFT did not write is simply ABSENT, so use getattr with a default. Energies are in hartree; BigDFT.DoS.AU_eV converts to eV.
intent: Read the energy and the main quantities of a finished calculation.
output:
energy          : -17.20985643 Ha = -468.3040 eV
atoms, orbitals : 3 4

description: Three things to look at: the last wavefunction residue against the criterion (dft.gnrm_cv), the warnings (log.log["WARNINGS"], absent or None when there are none), and that an energy is there at all. A run can end normally, report convergence, and still carry warnings worth reading.
intent: Check that a finished run converged, and collect what BigDFT warned about.
output:
h2o          : 11 iterations, residue 7.0e-05 <= 1.0e-04
pbe0_restart : 8 iterations, warnings: ['PSP generated with a different XC. Input XC is "XC: PBEH (PBE0)"']

description: The log of a relaxation holds one document per force evaluation: len(log) is their number (0 for a single point) and log[i] is step i. The attributes of the log itself (log.energy, log.forcemax) are those of the step of LOWEST ENERGY (log.reference_log), which is not necessarily the last one nor the one whose geometry BigDFT wrote in final_NAME.yaml.
intent: Read a geometry optimisation: take the LAST step, not the attributes of the log.
output:
Found 16 different runs

Found 16 different runs

description: BigDFT writes the final geometry in final_NAME.yaml (same directory as the log), with the forces on each atom. Keep the element and its position, drop the rest, and the result is a `posinp` dictionary for the next run.
intent: Start a calculation from the geometry a relaxation ended on.
output:
<BigDFT> log of the run will be written in logfile: ./log-after_relax.yaml
O-H distance after relaxation: 0.9779 angstroem

description: log.evals is a list with one BandArray per k-point. A BandArray is a numpy array of shape (number of spins, number of orbitals), in hartree. With spin polarisation the two rows may hold different numbers of orbitals: the shorter one is padded with nan. A log only holds occupied orbitals unless virtual states were asked for (extract_virtual_states).
intent: Read the orbital energies: highest occupied level, and both spins of a polarised system.

description: log.forces is a list, one dictionary per atom in the order of the input: {element: [fx, fy, fz]} in Ha/bohr. log.forcemax is the largest component norm.
intent: Read the forces on the atoms.

description: log.get_dos() returns a DoS built from the orbital energies, in eV. dump() gives two columns of text (energy, density); plot() draws on a matplotlib axis. Use the Agg backend where there is no display.
intent: Build the density of states of a run, as a table and as a figure.

points: 2500 | from -26.4 to -6.3 eV
written: dos.dat, dos.png

description: Read each log once into a dictionary NAME -> energy, skipping what is not finished, then apply the formula. Total energies are in hartree: 1 Ha = 27.2114 eV = 2625.50 kJ/mol = 627.51 kcal/mol.
intent: Compare two finished runs: an energy difference, converted, with missing runs handled.

description: If the wavefunction files are not where BigDFT looks (data-NAME/), it does not stop: it warns "Missing wavefunction files, switch to normal input guess" and starts from scratch. The run succeeds, with the same energy and more iterations. Only the warning tells.

description: Three steps. The earlier run must have written its orbitals (write_orbitals_on_disk): they are in data-EARLIER/, one file per orbital. The new run reads them from ITS OWN data directory, data-NEW/: copy the wavefunction-* files there. And its input says read_orbitals_from_disk(), which writes dft.inputpsiid = 2. Another functional or another grid spacing is fine.
